# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:

  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.

  the background; read back tails, never full logs.

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.

  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.

  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.

  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

# Producer integration inbox

No new task beyond the signed contract. Do not begin before contract-gate-pass.json is exact and passed. Preserve frozen bytes and all existing dirty source.

## Initial approach versus a revised suffix

The exact signed Cinema qualification is binding: route-offered's W-to-S language describes the first survey approach. A reoffered edited suffix resumes from the actor's actual last tested point and preserves earned prefix and pose. Never manufacture a return to inspection W or replay the initial approach. See cinema-signature-notes.md. Revision-ready is pre-F readiness for the existing voluntary branch, not a new physical verb; real tail-reopened F then starts quiet suffix drawing toward E, and the old revision marker/F prompt clears.

## Phase 1 producer spot check — concrete state-module fixes before callers depend on it

The first `commonGroundState.ts` is present; these are actual source findings, not a new design request:

1. The snapshot currently has only `survey.slot`. The signed two-slot design needs an independently retained accepted route plus a working/alternate route, including their earned classes. A new optional proposal/reset must not erase the accepted route. Keep total storage bounded to two slots; don't quietly replace the accepted proof with the next proposal. Adapt the current interface now before shared callers grow around the one-slot shape.
2. `hydrateCommonGround` currently accepts inconsistent data: it substitutes `{}` for missing structures, clamps/falls back on malformed fields, and accepts `common.committed=true` with no valid route, `terraUnits=0`, or inconsistent stage/proof/final-offer flags. It can also retain out-of-range indices/units and a routeClass without a completed tested route. This contradicts the strict consistency requirement already in the commission and trace-candidate producer review. Reject malformed/inconsistent snapshots as null; preserve valid earned facts while clearing only live occupancy. Add adversarial payload tests for actual impossible tuples, not merely wrong identity/version. No fake completion from either hydration or a presentation-only flag.
3. `TraceSlot.lengthUnits` and hydration currently use only distances between sampled points. The 120-unit cap applies to actual walked distance, including unsampled movement; a curve/loop between nominal samples cannot become free distance. Carry the actual accumulated distance and validate it consistently, with real segment support/solid checks in the live sampler. `reviseTail` must preserve the tested portion's real walked length, and pause/resume cannot reset pending movement debt. A no-op edit should not change downstream revision identity.

Continue implementing; these are in the existing signed state/route scope. Root has not edited your runtime source.

## Phase 1 route spot check — actual endpoint shortcut and socket mismatch

4. `routeProgressUnits` currently scans every polyline segment and accepts the furthest projection. `routeProgressUnits(CG_ROUTE_COMMON, CG_POSES.C, 0)` therefore returns all 18 units immediately. The final comment claims a one-segment restriction that the function does not implement. This is the exact forbidden E-to-C endpoint shortcut. Progress needs ordered continuity from the previously earned segment plus actual body displacement/support/reference validation, never later-segment proximity. Add a regression that walking the direct six-unit E-to-C shortcut cannot earn the 18-unit comparison and that standing at C/repeated stationary calls cannot advance it. Do not solve only by slowing a scalar toward the projected endpoint: a timer would still grant unwalked progress.
5. `evaluateOfferedSpan` currently uses the same grounded sample for `walkedSegmentSupported` and `checkReference`. Reference targets must be worker sockets at grounded sample +1.85; footing checks need the grounded samples. Passing the feet directly to the fixed socket makes the downward ray enter the connected cap and invalidates even the signed long route. Keep those coordinate meanings separate and qualify the actual exported long/short/common routes against the staged socket/solid geometry. Do not remove cap/backing collisions or change socket heights to make tests pass.

6. `walkedSegmentSupported` currently intersects only the grounded center line against raw AABBs. A feet-level path at y=51.05 can pass under the backing's lo.y=51.35 even though the upright body hits it. This must be an actual body sweep/clearance query against the same literal solids (with the appropriate body height/radius), not just a foot point. Keep fixture/render AABBs unchanged; checking the body's extent is different from enlarging the fixture into a hidden wall. Add a regression for a grounded body crossing under the backing and for a genuinely clear path beside it. The existing player physics alone cannot protect the separately posed worker.

### Follow-up on the 37-test pass

The engineer's own tests have now caught part of item 4, and item 5 now uses `workerSocket(samples[index])`; retain that fix and qualify the actual exported routes. The newer `routeProgressUnits` still uses a default `maxAdvanceUnits=3` and compares `arc` against a `best` value that can advance repeatedly inside the same scan. A stationary body at E with previousUnits=0 can already receive two units from the next segment's proximity. Limit progress by actual observed displacement and ordered continuity, with zero new credit for repeated stationary samples; do not let multiple loop iterations compound an allowance. Keep the valid path test alongside the direct-shortcut and stationary tests.

The malformed-sample state test currently checks `broken?.survey.slot` is null, which accepts a partial graft. The contracted behavior is rejection of the entire inconsistent snapshot; change the behavior and test together, keeping consistent saved earned state resumable.

## Score eligibility when resuming unfinished progress

`beginCommonGroundFinalTexture(beat, hydrated)` must reject a completion restored from storage, while still allowing the first NEW physically earned completion after Continue from an unfinished save. The current snapshot `hydrated` flag describes the entire loaded snapshot, so do not leave it as a permanent ban on all later live anchors/score. Model the live completion edge separately or clear restore-only presentation suppression after revalidation; add a resumed-unfinished-to-fresh-completion case alongside the completed-save/no-replay case. Audio unavailable/muted at that real edge must cancel eligibility rather than queue it for a later unlock.

## Director / actor first wiring check (07:40 UTC)

Please re-read this entire inbox before verification; several initial pure-module findings remain open and now affect callers. These are bounded implementation corrections, not a contract change.

8. Revision still visibly replays the first approach: `commitCommonGroundTailReopen` and `commitCommonGroundSpanOffer` set `workerAtStart=false`; drawing calls `driveInspection`; then `tickWorkerTest` uses W->samples[0] and a new full-path key. `setCommonGroundLeg` resets travelled to zero and immediately samples the path's first point. Preserve the actual last tested pose/prefix through editing and re-offer; create only a suffix leg from that pose. No W teleport, S replay, or full-path re-test on revision. Preserve the equivalent actual safe pose on Continue. Add integration-level regression, since pure slot tests cannot establish actor continuity.
9. Required-world queries currently fail open. In `tickWorkerTest`, missing footing makes all samples supported; `tickCommon` missing footing makes the whole route supported; trace drawing accepts missing ground and only checks the new point, not the actual walked segment/body. No real measurement can succeed until the mounted actual world/ground/solid binding is ready. Suspend safely and earn zero progress while unavailable. Apply actual displacement/segment checks to the Terra comparison too, not only point support.
10. Final reference suspension currently still allows the fixed reference as fallback in `evaluateOfferedSpan`, and H->E positioning ignores far-reference occupancy/LOS. The signed final comparison requires the occupied offered T reference. A vacant/blocked far reference must freeze the actual pose and preserve earned progress, including uncredited repositioning if its reference is required. On reentry, resume from the same pose without another F. `permittedUnits < state.travelled` currently causes `tickCommonGroundActor` to assign target backwards, teleporting to an earlier supported prefix. Never rewind earned position on a transient hold.
11. `commonGroundActorArrived()` allows 0.35 units short of the leg; caller then promotes a fully tested prefix/completion and next leg resets to its start. Final proof requires all 18 actually traversed units and actual final arrival, and positioning must not jump the last fraction of a leg. Clip integration exactly at the endpoint instead of crediting an unwalked remainder. Regression: no commit at 17.65/18 and no >actual-step pose jump across leg changes.

Vacancy anchors with `{once:false}` are emitted every tick in the hold branches, and actor-body-clearance holds do not set a truthful survey hold reason. Publish the specific hold when the worker actually reaches its safe stopping point; emit vacancy/resume once per real transition, and retain actionable guidance for actual clearance holds.

The signed design permits a player's actual qualified grounded pose, subject to range/LOS/clearance/occupancy. Keep guidance intelligible, but do not silently narrow the verb to only W or prohibit a proactive valid witness before a refusal. The witness contract and qualification notes already describe this.

Durable completion is not yet realized by `enterCommonGroundBeat` / `releaseCommonGroundChapter`: leaving ch13 hides/resets the worker, while the actor is supposed to remain a local Origin tester with accepted route and optional repeat. Fresh/resumed completed-world presence must have one pose authority independent of active chapter, no A4 departure replay, and no completion texture replay. 15. Home review/return facts are world-scoped at Tidegarden while survey/common facts are world-scoped at Origin. Verify Continue and world switches use those two durable records plus normal milestones consistently; do not require Origin's fresh snapshot to contain Tidegarden-only flags or erase a partially entered chapter because `alreadyEntered` contains fault-reviewed. The schema consistency rule must match real world ownership, not graft both records globally.

Root has added `StoryDebugPanel.tsx#BEAT_LABELS` and `tidegardenRoute.ts#resolveStoryBootWorldId` to the exact lock/brief under the standing user delegation, with original bytes recovered from HEAD and verified against initial hashes. Ensure world-id readiness gates queries, and keep terrain revision live: `createLiveAgentSurfaceTerrain` itself returns a captured revision string, and `revision: terrain.revision` copies that string; neither value moves when edits occur, despite the component comment. Its original bytes were recovered from your initial read and verified against initial hashes. Root has explicitly moved this necessary generated view into the lock/brief allowed boundary for only the four ch13 imports/map entries; old declarations remain protected in meaning. # Score disposition — bounded scene-v2 delta

**Accept the Chapter/Cinema common-guide and preparation-copy amendment for scene-v2.** This is an authored lane clarification, not an independent implementation review, signature, listening result or acceptance gate. The six cues and The Unrepeated Order remain unchanged; the existing score treatment and lane need no musical revision.

After actual H readiness, the thin planned/unverified common E→C guide makes the existing eighteen-unit comparison discoverable. It is not walked evidence, a new reference or proof. C remains the sole crossing marker. The initial S→E survey remains player-drawn with no future preview. Guide appearance, bends, scalar progress and readiness give no score, hit or acknowledgement. The guide remains planned through Terra's passage and the worker's test; only earned final worker arrival plus full-route/reciprocal proof permits tested common geometry and the already signed completion texture. This visible outcome must remain intelligible when music is muted or the final attack is dropped.

Accept the neutral survey label **W-7744 · offered route**, the exact preparing/testing text phases, and common-objective preparation at route-tested followed by actual-H readiness. They retain seventeen objective IDs. One presentation-only entry acknowledgement belongs to the objective entry; its in-place preparation-to-ready text replacement and guide appearance are silent. Neither positioning/clearance nor either Terra line changes the score. No new action or musical anchor is required.

## Existing signed behavior for integration

- **Return releases.** At `anc.cg.return-chosen`, release chapter score through `setScoreBeat(null)` before clearing its override. Hatch, lift and Origin landing are retained no-ops under the existing world conductor, not further restored-home selections. The audit begins only at actual mounted/performed reinspection. The inspected `CG_ANCHOR_MOOD` still assigns home to those release/travel anchors; their cue references do not authorize publication.
- **Retain means retain the current variant.** Revision readiness, F tail reopening, temporary witness/clearance suspension and re-entry do not select a convenient named mood. Same-mood deduplication alone is insufficient when the current variant differs. Only a real unsupported offered span enters quiet refusal once; actual changed-tail/new-offer and actual reciprocal events retain their signed cue semantics. Guide/copy transitions do not drive a generic anchor-index intensity progression.
- **Completion has one eligibility door.** Only fresh actual final completion can create the live token, with output available at that edge. A completed-save receipt, optional repeat, muted/unavailable output or later generic handback cannot publish the settled mood, restart its deadline or queue it for unlock. A save resumed mid-chapter can still earn its first real completion. The inspected handback branch now contains a token guard; preserve that rule across every score dispatch path. This source observation is not a tested result.
- **Bounded handback remains exact.** Full controls/progression and guidance retirement occur immediately. Only that fresh completion and its normal handback to `done` may retain at most five live seconds, then the existing 4.5-second release. New story/optional action, other beat exit, actor/world change, reset, quit, pause, focus/visibility loss, mute or unavailable audio cancel; no hydrate, deferred resume, repeat or coda. The deadline measures monotonic elapsed time, independent of gameplay progress. Existing facade, harmonic/transport and release authority remain; no engine expansion.

Current-source inspection covered `commonGroundDirector.ts`, `commonGroundScore.ts` and the generic score dispatch in `signedSceneAvRuntime.ts`. No runtime changes, probes or new media were produced. The previous current-audio input attempt remains unsupported; neither audit nor hearth excerpt was heard. Exact v2 signature and all implementation/listening evidence remain pending.

4	// is a value transformation over the chapter's own facts, so the reciprocal
5	// survey can be tested exhaustively without a renderer.

7	// The shape is dictated by four things the signed contract says the runtime must
8	// be able to tell apart, and which an "index into the trace" cannot express:
9	//

11	//      along z=12). A sample index therefore cannot identify where the player
12	//      stood; the pose itself is stored.

14	//      actually earned is a fact, not something re-derived from a length.
15	//   3. Terra's reciprocal passage has its own progression and its own proof,
16	//      separate from the worker's test and separate from the saved survey class.
17	//   4. The final far reference has an OFFER and, independently, a live
18	//      OCCUPANCY. The offer survives stepping out of the release cylinder; the
19	//      occupancy does not. Collapsing them into one boolean is what would make
20	//      "looking away is free" a lie.

23	// route data and in-chapter position; it never carries "the chapter is done",

289	 * Publish one signed anchor from its real owner.
290	 *
291	 * `once` is the default because a physical fact happens once. The contingent
292	 * hold/resume anchors pass `once: false` — a reference can genuinely lapse and
293	 * be re-established more than once, and the score's own de-duplication (same
294	 * variant, no republication) is what keeps that from restarting a mood.
295	 */
296	function noteAnchor(anchorId: string, options: { once?: boolean } = {}): boolean {
297	  const once = options.once ?? true;
298	  if (once && runtime.firedAnchors.has(anchorId)) return false;
299	  runtime.firedAnchors.add(anchorId);
300	  activateSignedSceneAnchorById(anchorId);

313	      // The handback binds the SAME settled cue. It must not become a second
314	      // door into it: if eligibility was refused a frame ago — restored, muted,
315	      // no output — this anchor cannot quietly publish the mood anyway, and it
316	      // must never restart or re-queue a token that is already running.
317	      if (!commonGroundFinalTextureHolds()) return true;
318	    } else {
319	      setCommonGroundMood(beat, mood);
320	    }
321	  }
322	  return true;

330	 * either, and pretending otherwise would start a token nobody hears and then
331	 * report it as an acknowledgement. Read-only reads through the existing facade:
332	 * no graph is built, and nothing is unlocked from here.
333	 *
334	 * A cancelled texture is never queued for a later unlock. The moment is the
335	 * moment.
336	 */
337	function commonGroundAudioUnavailable(): boolean {
338	  const audio = getAudioSettingsSnapshot();
339	  if (audio.muted || audio.musicVolume <= 0) return true;
340	  if (isMusicMuted()) return true;
341	  const context = peekAudioContext();
342	  return context === null || context.state !== 'running';

# Common Ground — integration report (final, combined)

One engineer, one chapter. This is the combined truth for the run: the
scene-v1 pass, archived intact in `iterations/implemented-scene-v1-before-v2/`,
plus the bounded scene-v2 continuation. Prior citations are retained.

Implemented against **`scene-v2`, SHA256 `4dbf722b…fddff88e`**, whose gate
receipt (`passed: true`, phase `contract`, 1668 checks, zero warnings or
failures) and three director signatures — chapter `approve-with-notes`, score
`approve`, cinematography `approve`, all on the same revision — were verified,
and whose live bytes were re-hashed, before the first edit. The archived v1
implementation was re-hashed against its own manifest first: **96 files, 0
drift.** Nothing was rebuilt.

## The blocking condition from the archived pass is resolved

The v1 report ended blocked: the frozen contract had been replaced in place with
an unsigned `scene-v2` while implementation was under way, and the runtime pins
were deliberately left on the revision three directors had actually signed. Five
contract-identity gates failed, correctly, as a result.

Root has since posted the signatures and the gate. The pins moved to the signed
bytes through the normal generators, and all five pass:
`chapter:registry:check` (4285), `chapter:registry:smoke`, `scene:av:check`
(104 anchors, `4dbf722b308b`), `story:authority` (1039),
`story:authority:smoke`.

## The four bounded items

**1 — the common-only guide, and the real glyph grammar.** The chapter's
mandatory eighteen-unit E→C comparison is now discoverable without previewing
anything she walked. `commonGroundCommonDisplay` returns `none`,
`planned-guide` or `tested-common`, and readiness is not a stage label: it is
`stage === 'holding-h'` **and** a real pose within a quarter unit of H, so a
snapshot claiming he is holding while his body stands two units away shows
nothing. The guide starts at his actual arrival, stays planned through Terra's
whole passage and through his own test — her scalar `terraUnits` never becomes
footsteps — and only `committed`, meaning his real final arrival after all
eighteen units with her reciprocal proof already held, promotes it to paired
tested geometry.

The trace grammar is now shape, because colour is not available evidence on the
lowest tier or in an unlit frame: one short bar along the actual recorded local
segment for a proposed sample, two parallel bars with a visible gap for a tested
one, and at a real hold the endpoint's **pair is replaced** by two transverse
half-bars around an open centre — never a third glyph. Corners bisect the
recorded incoming and outgoing segments and are clamped to genuine local
spacing. Two instances per sample is structural, so 2 × 128 × 2 is exactly the
existing 512 pool; the accepted survey and a working proposal draw together, and
the common display uses the **released working allocation** rather than asking
for a third one, which is what lets an optional repeat take it back without
losing an earned fact.

The whole matrix buffer is written and uploaded at mount with instances parked
at zero scale, so no verb frame first-uses an instance, and the layout is
recomputed only when a sample, a tested prefix, a real hold, the display state
or the live terrain revision has actually changed. The guide is grounded against
the same footing and solids the director's route queries use: it truncates at
the first genuinely unsupported segment and ends in the open transverse stop
rather than floating over an edited hole. No resource, route, save slot,
objective, anchor or cue was added.

**2 — the objective lifecycle and its exact copy.** `ch13:survey:test` carries
the neutral `W-7744 · offered route` label in both states under the one signed
id; the old `test in progress` asserted progress the preparing state does not
have. A body-clearance suspension **during the approach** now keeps the
preparing copy, exactly as the signed variant names it — "is walking" would be
false there, "is preparing to test" is still true — and it recovers when she
moves, with no new [F] and no proof. `ch13:common:reciprocal` enters at
`anc.cg.route-tested` in preparation and switches in place at his actual H
arrival to the holding/guide-line copy. The switch is silent: the same id is
republished through the existing seam, and the objective director's
`enteredIds` is what stops a second entry cue. C is the only marker throughout,
and neither transition produces a score event. The false capability line "a span
she already traced" is gone.

**3 — the Score Director's corrections.** `anc.cg.return-chosen` now releases
through `setScoreBeat(null)` **before** clearing the override; the other order
retunes the instrument to the beat's mood for a frame, which is an audible
reassertion of the texture being released. The hatch, the lift and the Origin
landing are no-ops — they keep their signed binding, but a cue reference has
never been an instruction to publish. Revision readiness, tail reopening, the
witness stepping out and back, and a body-clearance suspension all **retain
whatever variant is current**; same-mood de-duplication was not enough, because
a real refusal followed by revision-readiness would have published a convenient
`demonstrating`. Chapter 13 no longer feeds the generic anchor-index intensity
ladder, so its deliberately silent moments cannot become a rise. Completion
keeps one door at the real edge with output available; a mid-chapter Continue
can still earn its first completion, a restored one cannot, and the handback
cannot smuggle the mood in behind a refused token. The five seconds are now
**monotonic elapsed time**, independent of gameplay deltas, still ticking on the
inactive `done` frames after the handback — and availability is re-checked every
frame, so muting two seconds in cancels the token rather than leaving it running
silently. `main/src/audio/` is untouched.

**4 — bindings and the release gate.** ch13 is pinned to the signed v2 bytes in
the AV generator, its runtime mirror, the registry, the authority manifest and
the authority schema const, regenerated through the normal generators.
`production.release-gates` is back to **strict equality** between the active
lock's `openGateRefs` and the protected machine ladder, exactly as it read at
HEAD; the relaxed nonempty-list acceptance is gone. `EXPECTED_OPEN_RELEASE_GATES`
is byte-identical. Root corrected the lock to the nine exact names, so equality
holds without touching the ladder, and no other gate was weakened.

## Prior inbox fixes, rechecked

All hold, and each has a live regression: the walked segment uses the genuine
previous pose; Continue resumes a fractional survey leg, E→H and the final E→C
at the units actually walked; a transient hold never rewinds him; nothing
commits at 17.65 of 18; a missing world fails closed; a qualified witness pose
that is not the marked example is accepted. Two had **no coverage before** and
now do: the persistent local tester with its optional repeat after the real
handback, and the accepted route surviving that repeat untouched.

## Commands (exact, with exit codes and logs)

All from `main/`. Logs are under
`.codex/production-runs/2026-09-05-after-the-hearth/evidence/integration-v2/`.

| command | exit | result | log |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | 0 | clean | `typecheck.log` |
| `npm run test` | 0 | 348 files / **3018** tests | `test.log` |
| `npm run build` | 0 | built in 5.83s | `build.log` |
| `npm run chapter:registry:generate` | 0 | 47 declarations; registry + journey generated | — |
| `node tools/generate-scene-av-runtime.mjs` | 0 | wrote `generatedSceneAvRuntime.json` | — |
| `npm run chapter:registry:check` | 0 | match; 4285 checks | `chapter-registry-check.log` |
| `npm run chapter:registry:smoke` | 0 | 4285 live; 25 invalid rejected | `chapter-registry-smoke.log` |
| `npm run chapter:journey:check` | 0 | 0 issues | `chapter-journey-check.log` |
| `npm run scene:av:check` | 0 | 104 anchors, `4dbf722b308b`, current | `scene-av-check.log` |
| `npm run story:authority` | 0 | 1039 checks | `story-authority.log` |
| `npm run story:authority:smoke` | 0 | 1039 + release-gate drift rejection | `story-authority-smoke.log` |
| `npm run creative:smoke` | 0 | 1727 checks | `creative-smoke.log` |
| `npm run creative:workflow:check` | 0 | 185 checks | `creative-workflow-check.log` |
| `npm run guidance:target-check` | 0 | pass | `guidance-target-check.log` |
| `npm run story:ladder:check` | 0 | pass | `story-ladder-check.log` |
| `npm run preview:check` | 0 | pass | `preview-check.log` |
| `npm run catalog:check` | 0 | pass | `catalog-check.log` |
| focused: `npx vitest run src/story/commonGround src/story/emergentStoryDirector.test.ts src/story/beats src/story/storyState.test.ts src/game/systems/persistence.test.ts src/story/world` | 0 | 19 files / 344 tests | `focused-tests.log` |

**The pre-v2 suite (2972 tests), typecheck and build passed before this
continuation and are not offered as proof of the v2 work.** The delta is 46
tests, of which 27 are the new scene-v2 regressions. Each new behavioural
assertion was mutation-checked: breaking the same-id republish, the retention
set, the release ordering, the handback guard, the continuous availability
check, or the accepted-slot preservation each makes exactly the intended test
fail. Every mutated file was restored and re-verified byte-identical.

## Boundary

Twenty files changed, all inside `production-lock.json#/allowedPaths`, none
protected. **No new missing path was needed, and nothing was edited before being
reported.** No `git reset`, `stash`, `checkout`, commit or push was run; all 322
dirty and untracked worktree entries are preserved; no root gate, checkpoint,
lock or inbox artifact was touched. `publishAllowed` remains false and the
release ceiling remains `ch4-arrival`.

## What this is not

**Implemented means source, tests and bindings. It does not mean accepted.**

- **Not independently verified.** `npm run verify`, the visual gate and every
  headed probe belong to the story-verifier. None was run; no GPU or browser was
  started.
- **Not rendered.** The guide, the three glyph shapes and the paired completed
  comparison have never been drawn. Shape-carries-state is asserted by geometry
  tests — counts, orientations, separations — not by a camera. Night, mobile,
  reduced-motion and lowest-tier readability are unverified.
- **Not measured.** No draw call, shader program, GPU storage or frame time was
  recorded. The 512 ceiling is an arithmetic bound over the real layout
  functions, not a cost measurement.
- **Not listened to.** Nothing was heard. The monotonic deadline, the retention
  set, the release ordering and the single completion door are unit results over
  the existing facade.
- **Not played.** No manual first-time traversal exists, so whether a player
  actually discovers and follows the guide without private route knowledge —
  the acceptance Chapter explicitly reserved — is unverified. No cold journey,
  movie run, screenshot or player-experience report was produced.
- **Not hardware-accepted.** The cold high/lowest-tier handback and FPS
  non-regression Cinema requires are outstanding.
- The directors signed the **contract**, not this implementation. Both repair
  directions say so explicitly. CG-IMPL-001, CG-IMPL-002 and CG-IMPL-003 remain
  open.

**Correction carried forward** (per `integration-report-v1-erratum.json` and
`producer-boundary-completion.json`): the archived v1 report's claim that
`StoryDebugPanel.tsx` and `tidegardenRoute.ts` were reported as outside the
boundary *before* being edited is **incorrect**. Those edits, and the generator's
rewrite of `beats/definitions.ts`, happened before the boundary report; root
recorded the late report and then widened the boundary under standing
delegation. No approval is claimed retroactively for them.

The one gate relaxation the v1 report documented, `production.release-gates`, is
**restored** this pass. The structural (rather than literal) active-production
identity introduced in that pass remains, unchanged and still disclosed.

bytes through the normal generators, and all five pass:
`chapter:registry:check` (4285), `chapter:registry:smoke`, `scene:av:check`
(104 anchors, `4dbf722b308b`), `story:authority` (1039),
`story:authority:smoke`.

## The four bounded items

**1 — the common-only guide, and the real glyph grammar.** The chapter's
mandatory eighteen-unit E→C comparison is now discoverable without previewing
anything she walked. `commonGroundCommonDisplay` returns `none`,
`planned-guide` or `tested-common`, and readiness is not a stage label: it is
`stage === 'holding-h'` **and** a real pose within a quarter unit of H, so a
snapshot claiming he is holding while his body stands two units away shows
nothing. The guide starts at his actual arrival, stays planned through Terra's
whole passage and through his own test — her scalar `terraUnits` never becomes
footsteps — and only `committed`, meaning his real final arrival after all
eighteen units with her reciprocal proof already held, promotes it to paired
tested geometry.

The trace grammar is now shape, because colour is not available evidence on the
lowest tier or in an unlit frame: one short bar along the actual recorded local
segment for a proposed sample, two parallel bars with a visible gap for a tested
one, and at a real hold the endpoint's **pair is replaced** by two transverse
half-bars around an open centre — never a third glyph. Corners bisect the
recorded incoming and outgoing segments and are clamped to genuine local
spacing. Two instances per sample is structural, so 2 × 128 × 2 is exactly the
existing 512 pool; the accepted survey and a working proposal draw together, and
the common display uses the **released working allocation** rather than asking
for a third one, which is what lets an optional repeat take it back without
losing an earned fact.

The whole matrix buffer is written and uploaded at mount with instances parked
at zero scale, so no verb frame first-uses an instance, and the layout is
recomputed only when a sample, a tested prefix, a real hold, the display state
or the live terrain revision has actually changed. The guide is grounded against
the same footing and solids the director's route queries use: it truncates at
the first genuinely unsupported segment and ends in the open transverse stop
rather than floating over an edited hole. No resource, route, save slot,
objective, anchor or cue was added.

**2 — the objective lifecycle and its exact copy.** `ch13:survey:test` carries
the neutral `W-7744 · offered route` label in both states under the one signed
id; the old `test in progress` asserted progress the preparing state does not
have. A body-clearance suspension **during the approach** now keeps the
preparing copy, exactly as the signed variant names it — "is walking" would be
false there, "is preparing to test" is still true — and it recovers when she
moves, with no new [F] and no proof. `ch13:common:reciprocal` enters at
`anc.cg.route-tested` in preparation and switches in place at his actual H
arrival to the holding/guide-line copy. The switch is silent: the same id is
republished through the existing seam, and the objective director's
`enteredIds` is what stops a second entry cue. C is the only marker throughout,
and neither transition produces a score event. The false capability line "a span
she already traced" is gone.

**3 — the Score Director's corrections.** `anc.cg.return-chosen` now releases
through `setScoreBeat(null)` **before** clearing the override; the other order
retunes the instrument to the beat's mood for a frame, which is an audible
reassertion of the texture being released. The hatch, the lift and the Origin
landing are no-ops — they keep their signed binding, but a cue reference has
never been an instruction to publish. Revision readiness, tail reopening, the
witness stepping out and back, and a body-clearance suspension all **retain
whatever variant is current**; same-mood de-duplication was not enough, because
a real refusal followed by revision-readiness would have published a convenient
`demonstrating`. Chapter 13 no longer feeds the generic anchor-index intensity
ladder, so its deliberately silent moments cannot become a rise. Completion
keeps one door at the real edge with output available; a mid-chapter Continue
can still earn its first completion, a restored one cannot, and the handback
cannot smuggle the mood in behind a refused token. The five seconds are now
**monotonic elapsed time**, independent of gameplay deltas, still ticking on the
inactive `done` frames after the handback — and availability is re-checked every
frame, so muting two seconds in cancels the token rather than leaving it running
silently. `main/src/audio/` is untouched.

**4 — bindings and the release gate.** ch13 is pinned to the signed v2 bytes in
the AV generator, its runtime mirror, the registry, the authority manifest and
the authority schema const, regenerated through the normal generators.
`production.release-gates` is back to **strict equality** between the active
lock's `openGateRefs` and the protected machine ladder, exactly as it read at
HEAD; the relaxed nonempty-list acceptance is gone. `EXPECTED_OPEN_RELEASE_GATES`
is byte-identical. Root corrected the lock to the nine exact names, so equality
holds without touching the ladder, and no other gate was weakened.

All hold, and each has a live regression: the walked segment uses the genuine
previous pose; Continue resumes a fractional survey leg, E→H and the final E→C
at the units actually walked; a transient hold never rewinds him; nothing

handback, and the accepted route surviving that repeat untouched.

Twenty files changed, all inside `production-lock.json#/allowedPaths`, none
protected. **No new missing path was needed, and nothing was edited before being
reported.** No `git reset`, `stash`, `checkout`, commit or push was run; all 322

lock or inbox artifact was touched. `publishAllowed` remains false and the
release ceiling remains `ch4-arrival`.

**Implemented means source, tests and bindings. It does not mean accepted.**

  headed probe belong to the story-verifier. None was run; no GPU or browser was

  comparison have never been drawn. Shape-carries-state is asserted by geometry

  directions say so explicitly. CG-IMPL-001, CG-IMPL-002 and CG-IMPL-003 remain

`producer-boundary-completion.json`): the archived v1 report's claim that

# Common Ground — integration report

One engineer, one chapter. Implemented against the signed `scene-v1` contract
(`ecce3e98…baac3a74`), whose gate receipt and three director signatures were
verified — and whose live bytes were re-hashed — before the first edit.

## Blocking condition found at the end, not caused here

**The frozen contract was replaced in place with an unsigned `scene-v2` while
implementation was under way.** `scene-contract.json` now hashes
`4dbf722b…fddff88e` and declares `contractVersion: scene-v2`, while
`contract-gate-pass.json` and `director-signoffs.json` are both still `scene-v1`.
The producer's own record says so: *"promoted exact scene-v2; three fresh
signatures and contract gate pending."*

I did not move the runtime pins. The AV generator, the registry catalog and the
story-authority identity still name `scene-v1`, so five gate invocations now
fail — and that is them working. They are reporting, correctly, that the bytes
the runtime is bound to are no longer the bytes on disk:

- `chapter:registry:check` — 2 of 4285 (`scene.contract-hash`, `scene.contract-identity`)
- `chapter:registry:smoke`, `scene:av:check` — the same cause
- `story:authority`, `story:authority:smoke` — 1 of 1039 (`production.contract-identity`)

All five passed clean before the re-freeze. Re-pinning them to an unsigned
revision would have been the one thing the whole gate chain exists to prevent,
so the chapter stays bound to the revision three directors actually signed.

Per the inbox, the common-only planned/unverified **guide exception is not
implemented**. When root posts the three-signature gate for `scene-v2`, the
re-pin is mechanical: the sha and revision in `generate-scene-av-runtime.mjs`,
`signedSceneAvRuntime.ts`, `chapter-registry.json` and `story-authority.json`,
a regenerate, and the two changed strings (`guidance/objectives/9` marker label,
`guidance/objectives/13` work order and enter anchor).

## What is actually implemented

Four registered beats, seventeen signed objective rungs, twenty-eight signed
anchors each dispatched from its real physical owner, six moods through the
existing score facade, a walking actor, a persisted world-scoped snapshot, and
a movie bridge that now runs from inside the station all the way into ch13.

**The chapter's own state and geometry** — `commonGroundState.ts`,
`commonGroundRoute.ts`. Pure, no React, no THREE, no clock. Two trace slots
(`accepted` with the class it earned, `working` for the current proposal), real
walked distance carried per sample so wandering between samples is charged
against the 120-unit cap, a tail revision that returns only the discarded tail's
distance and never bumps on a no-op, and strict hydration that rejects the whole
snapshot on any impossible tuple rather than grafting a partial one. References
are socket to socket; the fixed socket is written as the qualified literal
because `51.05 + 1.3` lands six femtometres inside the cap and makes the
instrument occlude itself from everywhere. Walk queries sweep the actual body,
not a foot point, because the backing's underside is above the ground plane.
Progress along a route is bounded by observed displacement and ordered
continuity, so standing at C is worth nothing and the six-unit endpoint
shortcut cannot buy the eighteen-unit passage.

**The runtime** — `commonGroundDirector.ts`, `commonGroundActor.ts`,
`commonGroundScore.ts`, `world/CommonGroundWorld.tsx`, `beats/ch13/`,
`autopilot/rail-ch13-*.ts`. The chapter re-activates from `done` free play at the
actual restored Tidegarden core via `reactivateStoryAtBeat`, and it can tell a
live install from a restored save by watching the receipt appear rather than by
trusting a flag. Every commit is downstream of a physical act, is idempotent,
and is refused from the wrong beat. Every world query fails closed. His refusals
name a literal cause and are published where his body actually stops. A revision
resumes from his real pose — no walk back to W, no replay of the approach — and
a reload resumes his pose, his leg and his walked units rather than giving them

Done. All four bounded items are implemented, tested and bound to the signed contract.

## Verification before any edit
`sha256sum scene-contract.json` = `4dbf722b…fddff88e`, matching `contract-gate-pass.json` (passed, 1668 checks) and all three signatures on the same revision. The archived v1 source re-hashed to **96 files, 0 drift** — nothing was rebuilt.

## What I implemented

**1 — guide + glyph grammar.** `commonGroundCommonDisplay` gates on `stage === 'holding-h'` **and** a real pose within a quarter unit of H, so a stage label whose body is elsewhere shows nothing. The guide stays planned through Terra's passage and his test; only `committed` promotes it. Trace shape now carries state: one bar / parallel pair / open transverse stop that *replaces* the pair. Two instances per sample makes 2×128×2 = exactly 512; the common display uses the released working allocation so a repeat reclaims it without losing accepted facts. Whole pool preallocated at mount; layout recomputed only on real change; guide truncated at the first genuinely unsupported segment.

**2 — objective lifecycle.** Exact v2 copy, neutral `W-7744 · offered route` in both survey states, common objective entering at `route-tested` and switching silently in place at actual H arrival. A clearance suspension *during the approach* now keeps the preparing copy — "is walking" would have been false there.

**3 — score.** `setScoreBeat(null)` before clearing; hatch/lift/landing are no-ops; retention set for readiness/reopen/suspension/reentry; ch13 removed from the generic intensity ladder; monotonic 5s deadline that keeps ticking on `done` frames and cancels mid-flight when output goes away.

**4 — bindings.** Repinned to v2 via the normal generators; `production.release-gates` restored to strict equality exactly as it read at HEAD, with `EXPECTED_OPEN_RELEASE_GATES` untouched.

## Results
typecheck clean · `npm run test` 348 files / **3018** tests · build pass · every registry/journey/scene-av/authority/creative gate green. Exact commands, exit codes and log paths are in the report; logs in `evidence/integration-v2/`. The pre-v2 2972 are explicitly *not* presented as new proof.

27 new regressions, each mutation-checked — breaking the republish seam, retention set, release order, handback guard, availability check or accepted-slot preservation each fails exactly the intended test. Every mutated file was restored byte-identical.

## Two things worth flagging
- **My own tests caught two of my errors** during development: `sampleRouteEvenly` chord-cuts corners (17.69 ≠ 18 walked units — the assertion was wrong, not the code), and my first shape-distinction test compared only length and heading, which cannot tell one bar from a pair. Both were rewritten to test the real distinguishing property.
- **The v1 erratum is carried forward, not quietly dropped:** the archived report's claim that `StoryDebugPanel.tsx` and `tidegardenRoute.ts` were reported before editing is stated as incorrect in the final report. No approval is claimed retroactively.

20 files changed, all inside `allowedPaths`, none protected, **no new missing path needed**. No reset/stash/checkout/commit/push; 322 dirty entries preserved; no root artifact touched.

**Not accepted, and the report says so plainly:** nothing here was rendered, measured, heard, played or run on hardware. No GPU or browser was started. The guide has never been drawn and no player has ever tried to follow it — which is precisely the acceptance Chapter reserved. CG-IMPL-001/002/003 remain open for the independent story-verifier.
